questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Having or showing the ability to speak fluently and coherently
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'articulate'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Being **articulate** means being able to express oneself clearly and well. 

 
 
• Example- She gave the police an **articulate** account of the incident.
 
 
 
• It is clear that **'articulate'** is the most appropriate choice for the one-word substitution of the given set of words.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hesitant **means being reluctant to do something.

 
 
• Example- He was **hesitant** to accept the offer.
 
 
 
• Being **inarticulate **means being unable to express one's ideas clearly or easily.
 
 
• Example- He is smart but somewhat** inarticulate**.
 
 
 
• **Incoherent **means expressed in an incomprehensible or confusing way.
 
 
• Example- He screamed some **incoherent **threat.

**Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.**

Uncouth
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Cultivated". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Let's examine each option:**

 
 
• **"Conspicuous" -** This term generally means something easily visible or noticeable; it doesn't directly refer to manners or refinement, so it's not an antonym of "uncouth," which refers to a lack of good manners, refinement, or grace.
 
• **"Barbaric" **- This describes behavior that is savage, cruel, or inhuman.
 
 
• This is closer to a synonym, rather than an antonym, for "uncouth."
 
 
 
• **"Cultivated" **- This word refers to something or someone refined, cultured, or well-educated.
 
 
• This is clearly an antonym of "uncouth," which describes someone who is lacking in sophistication, refinement, or manners.
 
 
 
• **"Covered" **- This word generally means something concealed or protected; it has no direct opposite link with "uncouth."
 
 
 
• Therefore, the most accurate antonym for **"uncouth" **from the given options is **"Cultivated".**
 
• In detail, **"uncouth" **refers to being awkward, clumsy, or lacking in sophistication or good manners.
 
• It often characterizes an individual who is uncultured, crude, or rough.
 
• Conversely, **"cultivated" **refers to a person who is well-educated, mannered, polished, and shows sophistication.
 
 
• It represents an individual who has been trained or influenced, often in terms of manners and taste, suggesting a refined and socially comfortable nature.
 
• This makes "cultivated" a suitable antonym for "uncouth".
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**

questions.question:
Which of the following sentences is/are grammatically correct among the three given below?

A. Despite of not knowing the outcomes, we pursue victory as we run.

B. Ramesh is advised to wait outside until the interviewer calls him.

C. Unless you do not study hard you will not pass.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Only **B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• Statement A:​

 
 
• Despite is used to link two contrasting ideas or show that one fact makes the other fact surprising.
 
• The sentence tells that we run for victory even if we don't know the results.
 
• 'of' is not with after 'despite'.
 
 
• For example: Your data is still safe, despite being locked up inside an otherwise nonbooting machine.
 
 
 
• Therefore, statement A is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct sentence should be: *Despite not knowing the outcomes, we pursue victory as we run.*
 
 
 
• ​Statement B:
 
 
• Until means 'up to the event mentioned'.
 
• We use 'until' when we are talking about time.
 
• The sentence tells that it is suggested to Ramesh to wait outside up to the time the interviewer calls.
 
• Therefore, statement B is grammatically correct.
 
 Statement C:

 
 
• We use the conjunction unless to mean 'except if'.
 
• ‘Unless’ expresses a condition, It is always used in the negative sense.
 
• It talks about a situation that could happen, or something that could be true, in the future.
 
• Thus, ‘not’ is never used with ‘unless’.
 
• Therefore, statement C is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct sentence should be: *Unless you study hard you will not pass.*
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: *Only B.*

questions.question:
Directions: Each item in this section has a sentence with three underlined parts labelled as (a), (b) and (c). Read each sentence to find out whether there is any error in any underlined part and indicate your response. on the Answer Sheet against the corresponding letter i.e., (a) or (b) or (c). If you find no error, your response should be indicated as (d). 

As the use of plastic becomes increasingly prevalent,(A)/ the problem of plastic waste(B)/ had become a major concern.(C)/ No error(D)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**C**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There is an error in **part (c)**. The correct **phrase** should be: "**has become a major concern**."
 
• The **verb** "**had become**" should be replaced with the **verb** "**has become**" because it is the **present perfect** form of the **verb** "**become**," which describes an **action that started in the past and continues to the present**.
 
• The **verb** "**become**" means "**to start to be**," and it is used to describe a change in status or condition.
 
• In this case, the problem of plastic waste started in the past and continues to be a major concern in the present, so the **present perfect** form is appropriate.
 
• The **past simple** form, "**had become**," describes an **action that was completed in the past** and is **no longer true or relevant in the present**, which does not fit the meaning of the sentence in this context.

Thus, ***option 3*** is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence**__: *As the use of plastic becomes increasingly prevalent, the problem of plastic waste **has become a major concern**. *

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

His wife has a bad __habit for accusing him__ for others' mistakes too.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is:** habit of accusing him**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct preposition to use after "**habit**" is "**of**."
 
• We talk about having a habit of doing something, not a habit for doing something.
 
 
• **For example**, "*a habit of reading*," "*a habit of exercising*."
 
 
 
• The correct structure is "**accusing him of**."
 
• When we accuse someone, we use "**of**" to indicate the offense or wrongdoing.
 
 
• **For example**, "*accusing him of stealing*," "*accusing her of lying*."
 
 
 
• So, the **corrected sentence** is: "*His wife has a bad habit of accusing him of others' mistakes too.*"
 
• This version maintains proper prepositions and accurately conveys that the wife has a habit of accusing her husband of mistakes that others have made.

Thus, **option 1** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage discusses the impacts of climate change, emphasizing the need for capacity to cope with its effects.
 
• The appropriate word should refer to the ability to adjust or deal with challenges, particularly in the face of climate change.
 
• **"Adaptive"** fits well as it relates to the capacity to adjust or respond to environmental changes, aligning with the context of climate change impacts.
 
• Other options ("adoptive", "minimum", "affective") do not convey the idea of adjusting to or coping with environmental challenges in the context of climate change.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Adoptive" **refers to taking on or accepting something, which does not fit the context of resilience or capacity in response to climate change.
 
• **"Minimum"** suggests a lowest amount or degree, which doesn't fit with the context of coping with climate impacts.
 
• **"Affective" **relates to emotions, which is not relevant to the context of climate adaptation or capacity.
